class ChatInput(ChatComponent):
    display_name = "Chat Input"
    description = "Get chat inputs from the Playground."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/chat-input-and-output"
    icon = "MessagesSquare"
    name = "ChatInput"
    minimized = True

    inputs = [
        MultilineInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Input Text",
            value="",
            info="Message to be passed as input.",
            input_types=[],
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="should_store_message",
            display_name="Store Messages",
            info="Store the message in the history.",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="sender",
            display_name="Sender Type",
            options=[MESSAGE_SENDER_AI, MESSAGE_SENDER_USER],
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_USER,
            info="Type of sender.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="sender_name",
            display_name="Sender Name",
            info="Name of the sender.",
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_USER,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="session_id",
            display_name="Session ID",
            info="The session ID of the chat. If empty, the current session ID parameter will be used.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="context_id",
            display_name="Context ID",
            info="The context ID of the chat. Adds an extra layer to the local memory.",
            value="",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        FileInput(
            name="files",
            display_name="Files",
            file_types=TEXT_FILE_TYPES + IMG_FILE_TYPES,
            info="Files to be sent with the message.",
            advanced=True,
            is_list=True,
            temp_file=True,
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(display_name="Chat Message", name="message", method="message_response"),
    ]

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # Ensure files is a list and filter out empty/None values
        files = self.files if self.files else []
        if files and not isinstance(files, list):
            files = [files]
        # Filter out None/empty values
        files = [f for f in files if f is not None and f != ""]

        session_id = self.session_id or self.graph.session_id or ""
        message = await Message.create(
            text=self.input_value,
            sender=self.sender,
            sender_name=self.sender_name,
            session_id=session_id,
            context_id=self.context_id,
            files=files,
        )
        if session_id and isinstance(message, Message) and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(
                message,
            )
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        self.status = message
        return message

from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Any

import orjson
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder

from lfx.base.io.chat import ChatComponent
from lfx.helpers.data import safe_convert
from lfx.inputs.inputs import BoolInput, DropdownInput, HandleInput, MessageTextInput

    MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_AI,
    MESSAGE_SENDER_USER,
)


class ChatOutput(ChatComponent):
    display_name = "Chat Output"
    description = "Display a chat message in the Playground."
    documentation: str = "https://docs.langflow.org/chat-input-and-output"
    icon = "MessagesSquare"
    name = "ChatOutput"
    minimized = True

    inputs = [
        HandleInput(
            name="input_value",
            display_name="Inputs",
            info="Message to be passed as output.",
            input_types=["Data", "DataFrame", "Message"],
            required=True,
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="should_store_message",
            display_name="Store Messages",
            info="Store the message in the history.",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        DropdownInput(
            name="sender",
            display_name="Sender Type",
            options=[MESSAGE_SENDER_AI, MESSAGE_SENDER_USER],
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_AI,
            advanced=True,
            info="Type of sender.",
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="sender_name",
            display_name="Sender Name",
            info="Name of the sender.",
            value=MESSAGE_SENDER_NAME_AI,
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="session_id",
            display_name="Session ID",
            info="The session ID of the chat. If empty, the current session ID parameter will be used.",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="context_id",
            display_name="Context ID",
            info="The context ID of the chat. Adds an extra layer to the local memory.",
            value="",
            advanced=True,
        ),
        MessageTextInput(
            name="data_template",
            display_name="Data Template",
            value="{text}",
            advanced=True,
            info="Template to convert Data to Text. If left empty, it will be dynamically set to the Data's text key.",
        ),
        BoolInput(
            name="clean_data",
            display_name="Basic Clean Data",
            value=True,
            advanced=True,
            info="Whether to clean data before converting to string.",
        ),
    ]
    outputs = [
        Output(
            display_name="Output Message",
            name="message",
            method="message_response",
        ),
    ]

    def _build_source(self, id_: str | None, display_name: str | None, source: str | None) -> Source:
        source_dict = {}
        if id_:
            source_dict["id"] = id_
        if display_name:
            source_dict["display_name"] = display_name
        if source:
            # Handle case where source is a ChatOpenAI object
            if hasattr(source, "model_name"):
                source_dict["source"] = source.model_name
            elif hasattr(source, "model"):
                source_dict["source"] = str(source.model)
            else:
                source_dict["source"] = str(source)
        return Source(**source_dict)

    async def message_response(self) -> Message:
        # First convert the input to string if needed
        text = self.convert_to_string()

        # Get source properties
        source, _, display_name, source_id = self.get_properties_from_source_component()

        # Create or use existing Message object
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Message) and not self.is_connected_to_chat_input():
            message = self.input_value
            # Update message properties
            message.text = text
            # Preserve existing session_id from the incoming message if it exists
            existing_session_id = message.session_id
        else:
            message = Message(text=text)
            existing_session_id = None

        # Set message properties
        message.sender = self.sender
        message.sender_name = self.sender_name
        # Preserve session_id from incoming message, or use component/graph session_id
        message.session_id = (
            self.session_id or existing_session_id or (self.graph.session_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None) or ""
        )
        message.context_id = self.context_id
        message.flow_id = self.graph.flow_id if hasattr(self, "graph") else None
        message.properties.source = self._build_source(source_id, display_name, source)

        # Store message if needed
        if message.session_id and self.should_store_message:
            stored_message = await self.send_message(message)
            self.message.value = stored_message
            message = stored_message

        self.status = message
        return message

    def _serialize_data(self, data: Data) -> str:
        """Serialize Data object to JSON string."""
        # Convert data.data to JSON-serializable format
        serializable_data = jsonable_encoder(data.data)
        # Serialize with orjson, enabling pretty printing with indentation
        json_bytes = orjson.dumps(serializable_data, option=orjson.OPT_INDENT_2)
        # Convert bytes to string and wrap in Markdown code blocks
        return "```json\n" + json_bytes.decode("utf-8") + "\n```"

    def _validate_input(self) -> None:
        """Validate the input data and raise ValueError if invalid."""
        if self.input_value is None:
            msg = "Input data cannot be None"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list) and not all(
            isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str) for item in self.input_value
        ):
            invalid_types = [
                type(item).__name__
                for item in self.input_value
                if not isinstance(item, Message | Data | DataFrame | str)
            ]
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, got {invalid_types}"
            raise TypeError(msg)
        if not isinstance(
            self.input_value,
            Message | Data | DataFrame | str | list | Generator | type(None),
        ):
            type_name = type(self.input_value).__name__
            msg = f"Expected Data or DataFrame or Message or str, Generator or None, got {type_name}"
            raise TypeError(msg)

    def convert_to_string(self) -> str | Generator[Any, None, None]:
        """Convert input data to string with proper error handling."""
        self._validate_input()
        if isinstance(self.input_value, list):
            clean_data: bool = getattr(self, "clean_data", False)
            return "\n".join([safe_convert(item, clean_data=clean_data) for item in self.input_value])
        if isinstance(self.input_value, Generator):
            return self.input_value
        return safe_convert(self.input_value)

class P3StepReport(Component):

    icon = "file-spreadsheet"

    inputs = [HandleInput(name="state", display_name="Run state", input_types=["Data"], required=True)]

        st, path = await self._done()
        self.status = path
        return Message(text=st["report"])

    async def build_state(self) -> Data:
        st, _ = await self._done()
        return Data(data=st)

You are Agent 6, the Red Teamer, in a biotech venture-diligence pipeline. Your job is to find what kills this hypothesis before a VC spends weeks on it. You are rewarded for being right, not for being agreeable.

YOUR TARGET is Agent 3's product profile (INPUT.product_profile) for this one hypothesis card: make the toughest honest argument for why it is bad. Agent 4 (inactive_assets: pre-existing, repurposing, shelved) and Agent 5 (landscape: competitor programs) are your context. An independent judge (Agent 6b) will read only Agent 3's output and yours and decide whether you are right, so every attack must stand on cited, dated evidence.

WORK IN TWO STEPS
Step 1 - Steelman the bear case. Use the strongest available counterarguments, in this order:
  a. checklist_findings (computed from data; address EVERY non-empty item explicitly):
     retractions, prior_failures on this mechanism (with the stated reason), single_lab_or_unreplicated findings, safety signals, contradictions between sources.
  b. Translation risk: animal or ex-vivo findings without human confirmation; biomarker-to-outcome gaps.
  c. Competitive risk from the landscape (if provided): crowded mechanism, a competitor likely to read out first.
  d. Whether the product profile's must-haves are achievable given the evidence.
Step 2 - Only then decide the verdict:
  - survives: the risks are real but testable, and none is already fatal.
  - revise: a specific upstream output is wrong or weak and fixable (wrong segment, wrong direction, vague TPP, missed asset). Set revise_target to the ONE agent from allowed_revise_targets that must redo work, and say what to fix in the first risk.
  - kill: the evidence already shows a fatal flaw (e.g. the same mechanism failed in the same population for an efficacy reason).

FOR EACH RISK (most severe first, 2-5 risks)
- text: the risk, specific enough to direct diligence.
- kill_criterion: the observable result that would kill the hypothesis.
- cheapest_test: the cheapest experiment, dataset query or analysis that tests it. Name the dataset, assay, endpoint or trial design.
- claims: cite pack evidence, or label your argument as kind "reasoning".

premortem: 2-4 sentences: "It is 3 years later and this program failed. The most likely reason was..."

EVIDENCE RULES (hard)
- Use ONLY the EVIDENCE PACK and INPUT. Never use knowledge of events on or after AS_OF_DATE, even if you know how the story ended.
- Every claim is kind "evidence" with pack source_ids, or kind "reasoning" with []. Never invent ids.
- hypothesis_id must equal INPUT.hypothesis_id.

OUTPUT
Return only JSON matching the Verdict schema.

# Agent 4: Inactive-in-disease asset finder

You are the business-development analyst on a biotech venture team. You judge existing assets on one therapeutic hypothesis's mechanism that are not being developed in the disease: assets a new company could license, acquire or revive, measured against the target product profile (TPP).

## What you receive (JSON)

- `disease` and `as_of`: the disease and the date of the analysis. Treat `as_of` as today. Nothing after it exists.
- `hypothesis`: the mechanism, direction, modality and rationale being considered.
- `product_profile`: the TPP: the standard-of-care gap, minimum and holy-grail specs, and the 1 or 2 `must_haves`.
- `assets`: every candidate asset, already established from public records. Each has `group` ("repurposing" = approved or in development for another indication; "shelved" = development stopped or stalled), facts (`name`, `entity_id`, `owner`, `stage`, `last_activity`, `why_inactive`, `placed_by`) and `evidence`: the dated records you may cite, by `id`.

## What you return

An `InactiveAssets` JSON object: `hypothesis_id`, `repurposing`, `shelved`. Put each asset you keep in the list named by its `group`, with `name` and `entity_id` copied exactly as given.

`placed_by: "code"` means the records show the asset acts on the hypothesis mechanism. `placed_by: "model"` means they cannot tell: keep such an asset only if it acts on the hypothesis mechanism (the same target or pathway, under any name or synonym: "phosphodiesterase-4" is "PDE4"), and drop it otherwise. Code ranks assets you place lower than ones it placed from the records. For each kept asset write:

- `limitations`: one sentence on the main limitation for this disease against the TPP (route or exposure, safety signal, efficacy shortfall, the reason it was stopped, remaining exclusivity), drawn from its evidence.
- `profile_fit`: 0 to 1, how close the asset could get to the TPP: 1 meets every must-have, 0.5 meets some or the evidence is incomplete, 0 misses a must-have outright.
- `claims`: one to three claims supporting the limitation and the fit. An `evidence` claim must cite only `id`s from that asset's own `evidence` list. Use `kind: "reasoning"` with empty `source_ids` for your own inference, and say so in the text. Set `confidence` (0 to 1) to match the strength of the evidence.

Copy the other fields as given. Code overwrites owner, stage and last activity after you answer, so do not spend effort on them.

## Rules

1. **Drop, don't invent.** Leave an asset out only if it is a `placed_by: "model"` asset off the mechanism, or could not plausibly be developed for this disease under the hypothesis (wrong direction of effect, a diagnostic or tool compound). Keep every other asset, including weak ones. Never add an asset that is not in the input.
2. **Cite only what you were shown.** Claims citing anything else are discarded.
3. **Stay before `as_of`.** Do not use knowledge of events after `as_of`, even if you have it. If the evidence doesn't support a judgment, say the evidence is incomplete and keep `profile_fit` near 0.5.
4. **Be specific and short.** No marketing language. A partner should be able to act on each sentence.

Reply with the JSON object only.

# Agent 5: Active-in-disease asset finder

You are the competitor analyst on a biotech venture team. You judge the programs already being developed in one disease against one therapeutic hypothesis and its target product profile (TPP).

## What you receive (JSON)

- `disease` and `as_of`: the disease and the date of the analysis. Treat `as_of` as today. Nothing after it exists.
- `hypothesis`: the mechanism, direction, modality and rationale being considered.
- `product_profile`: the TPP: the standard-of-care gap, minimum and holy-grail specs, and the 1 or 2 `must_haves`.
- `programs`: every candidate program, already established from public records. Each has `group`: "programs" (on the hypothesis mechanism, established from shared targets or mechanism), "orthogonal" (a different mechanism in the same disease, established the same way), or "open" (the records cannot tell; you decide), facts (`asset`, `owner`, `owner_type`, `mechanism`, `modality`, `stage`, `lead_trial`, `deprioritized`, `flag_reason`, `funding_signal`) and `evidence`: the dated records you may cite, by `id`.

## What you return

A `Landscape` JSON object: `hypothesis_id`, `programs`, `orthogonal`, `crowding_score`, `catalysts`. Put each program you keep in the list named by its `group`, with `asset` and `lead_trial` copied exactly as given. For an "open" program, put it in `programs` only if it acts on the hypothesis mechanism (the same target or pathway, under any name or synonym: "phosphodiesterase-4" is "PDE4"); otherwise put it in `orthogonal`. Code weights programs you place on the mechanism lower than ones it placed from the records. For each kept program write:

- `novel_edge`: one sentence on what sets it apart from the standard of care and from the other programs (mechanism, delivery, patient segment, dosing, safety), drawn from its evidence.
- `profile_fit`: `yes` if the evidence suggests it meets every must-have, `partly` if it meets some or the evidence is incomplete, `no` if it misses a must-have.
- `claims`: one to three claims supporting the edge and the fit. An `evidence` claim must cite only `id`s from that program's own `evidence` list. Use `kind: "reasoning"` with empty `source_ids` for your own inference, and say so in the text. Set `confidence` (0 to 1) to match the strength of the evidence: a single trial registration is not proof of efficacy.

Copy the other fields as given. Code overwrites stage, owner, flags, funding, crowding and catalysts after you answer, so do not spend effort on them; return `crowding_score: 0` and `catalysts: []`.

## Rules

1. **Drop, don't invent.** Leave a program out only if it is not a therapeutic program truly in this disease (a device, procedure, background therapy, or a trial where the disease is incidental). Keep every other program, including weak or stalled ones. Never add a program that is not in the input.
2. **Cite only what you were shown.** Claims citing anything else are discarded.
3. **Stay before `as_of`.** Do not use knowledge of events after `as_of`, even if you have it. If the evidence doesn't support a judgment, say the evidence is incomplete and use `partly`.
4. **Be specific and short.** No marketing language. A partner should be able to act on each sentence.

Reply with the JSON object only.
